A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Function-Space Learning Rates by the same authors and are readable, including their appendices. The original methods, experiments, and figures can be matched reliably to the retained material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original learning-rate and training-loss experiments on ResMLPs, transformers, and LoRA adapters in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds estimator diagnostics, test-loss results, and experiments with additional training configurations and optimizers.

M1.justification: Appendix D adds a readout-specific estimator exploiting independence between output rows and bias entries, evaluated in Figure 26. The core FLeRM procedure remains. Algorithm 1 also corrects its learning-rate ratio to base/current, agreeing with Equation 19 already present in v1; this does not establish that the original implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, Wikitext-103, Cold French Law, and MathPile for the same classification and language-modeling tasks. The added test-loss evaluations and model/optimizer sweeps retain this data and task coverage.

E2.justification: The width-transfer comparisons expand beyond standard Adam to momentum SGD, SignSGD/Signum, AdamW, Adamax, and Adagrad, each compared with its FLeRM counterpart (Figures 20–25). Figure 15 also newly compares the Kronecker estimator against IID and no-assumption estimators.

E3.justification: The original experimental settings are retained, but Appendices C.7–C.11 introduce test-loss evaluation, cosine scheduling, affine layernorm parameters, simultaneous width/depth scaling, and alternative optimizer settings. Figure 15 adds a first-training-step estimator evaluation using 10,000 batches.

E4.justification: v2 retains the periodic-update, equal-rate, and LoRA analyses and substantially expands diagnostics. New analyses examine covariance assumptions, generalization, sensitivity to schedules and layernorm configuration, joint scaling, optimizer robustness, and the effect of readout-specific variance reduction (C.6–C.11 and Appendix D).

E5.justification: Figure 15 newly reports empirical estimator bias and variance over 10,000 batches. This characterizes estimator variability rather than independent training-run uncertainty. The eight-seed base-model averaging and single-seed LoRA calibration remain unchanged, and the new performance plots do not add confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Figures 1–14 retain their results, while Figures 15–26 add substantial findings: the Kronecker estimator trades some bias for reduced variance, test-loss optima align more closely with FLeRM, additional optimizer/configuration comparisons support transfer, and readout-specific estimation reduces ResMLP curve noise. These are additional results under their stated settings.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds a localized mathematical extension: it derives readout-row and bias independence, corresponding simplified estimators, and equivalence of IID and diagonal assumptions for estimating the summed bias variances (Equations 29–35). The general Kronecker and tensor-normal derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: efficient function-space learning-rate measurement, analysis of optimizer dynamics, and FLeRM transfer across width, depth, initialization scale, and LoRA rank. The new experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: C.7 proposes overfitting as the explanation for imperfect ResMLP test-loss alignment, contrasting the single-epoch transformers. C.11 attributes noisy SGD curves to using SGD with transformers, supported by the smoother ResMLP experiment. These add specific interpretations without replacing the earlier conclusions.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses roughly 814M parameters for the retained widest transformer, explains cosine-schedule transfer through base-model learning-rate ratios, and supplies settings such as momentum 0.9 and AdamW weight decay 0.1. The original model/data details and code-access link remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Chizat and Bach, Sirignano and Spiliopoulos, and a comparison with Chizat and Netrapalli's feature-speed approach. It also softens the Everett discussion from violated alignment assumptions to difficulty choosing appropriate assumptions. The overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely unchanged. Limited edits clarify time-indexed matching and matrix dimensions, repair wording, and update publication footnotes. Acknowledgements and an impact statement are added, while new scientific material is organized into C.6–C.11 and Appendix D.

P2.justification: Figures 15–26 substantially expand the visual evidence with bias/variance bars and additional generalization, robustness, and estimator-comparison plots. Figures 1–14 retain their designs, with appendix figures relocated. Some new labeling is inconsistent, notably Figure 25's transformer plot label versus its ResMLP caption.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps in v1 through direct estimator bias/variance measurements, held-out losses, and robustness checks beyond constant-schedule Adam. It also corrects the pseudocode ratio and derives a tested readout-specific refinement. These additions substantially strengthen the evidence and reproducibility; minor new caption and labeling inconsistencies do not outweigh those gains.
